title: Begin with a clear question
summary: Data is recorded information. Data science uses careful questions and checks to learn from it. A clear question tells us what we need to count.
introduction: Data is recorded information. Data science uses careful questions and checks to learn from it. A clear question tells us what we need to count. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain begin with a clear question
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Data is recorded information. Data science uses careful questions and checks to learn from it. A clear question tells us what we need to count.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: Run Python examples in a separate Python 3 environment. They need only built-in libraries. Use fictional classroom data; do not collect names or private learner information for these exercises.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Data Science. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
Question: which book type was borrowed most this week?
Needed: one row per borrowing and the book type
Not needed: learner names or home addresses
Result: a count for each type
blocks.title: Begin with a clear question

blocks.text: The question asks about borrowing events. We can answer it without recording who borrowed each book.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Write a question about book returns and list only the data it needs.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Collecting extra personal details does not make an answer better.
For more detail later, use this [Data Science further reading](https://www.openintro.org/book/ims/).
